name: G6E-134P-ST-US-DC5
title: G6E: subminiature sensitive SPDT signal relay, 2 A 30 VDC, sealed PCB type, single-side stable or latching
summary: A small fully sealed through-hole relay with one SPDT contact (bifurcated crossbar, Ag with gold alloy) for switching signals and light loads: 2 A at 30 VDC or 0.4 A at 125 VAC resistive, 3 A carry. The standard coil needs about 200 mW (picking up at about 98 mW); an L variant and the 48 V coil take about 400 mW. It comes as a single-side stable type (G6E), a single-winding latching type (G6EU) and a double-winding latching type (G6EK), in 5 to 48 VDC coils, with -U variants that tolerate ultrasonic cleaning. Coil to contacts stands 1,500 VAC and a 2,500 V surge; it weighs about 2.7 g, runs from -40 to 70°C and carries UL and CSA approval. The G6E-134P-US DC5 is the 5 VDC single-side stable standard type: 40.0 mA, 125 Ω.
key_figures: 0.4 A at 125 VAC; 2 A at 30 VDC

notes: Code fields in order: G6E, then the relay function (nothing for single-side stable, U for single-winding latching, K for double-winding latching); after the dash, 1 for one pole SPDT (1c), 3 for the bifurcated crossbar Ag (Au-alloy) contact, 4 for fully sealed, P for PCB terminals, then nothing for the standard coil or L for the low-sensitivity (400 mW) coil; -US for UL and CSA approval; a final -U marks the type made for ultrasonic cleaning.
The rated coil voltage is added to the model number when ordering, for example G6E-134P-US DC5. On the case and the packing the coil voltage is marked in the form @@ VDC.
Approval files: UL E41515, CSA LR31928. All models are RoHS compliant.

circuits.title: Contact wiring for a DC load
circuits.description: A DC supply feeds the common contact, pin 7, from its positive side. One load hangs from the NO contact, pin 12, and another from the NC contact, pin 10; both return to the supply's negative side. Putting the common on the positive side lengthens contact life beyond the performance ratings, since the polarity across the contacts changes how much contact material moves.

parts.note: contacts only, pins 7, 10 and 12; the coil drive is separate

operation.text: Three coil systems share one SPDT contact and footprint. The single-side stable G6E holds its contacts only while the coil is energised. The single-winding latching G6EU has one coil: a pulse one way sets it, the opposite polarity resets it, and it stays put with no coil current. The double-winding latching G6EK has separate set and reset coils with a common negative terminal. Latching types need a pulse of at least 15 ms to set or reset.

The standard coil draws about 200 mW at rated voltage and picks up at about 98 mW. The L (low-sensitivity) coil and the 48 VDC standard coil draw about 400 mW. Every coil must operate (or set and reset) at 70% of rated voltage at most; single-side stable types release at 10% or more.

At 23°C a standard 200 mW coil may be given up to 190% of rated voltage and a 400 mW coil up to 170%. The permitted maximum falls in a straight line with ambient temperature, to about 130% and 116% of rated voltage at 70°C. This maximum is the top of the range over which the operating supply may vary, not a voltage to hold continuously. Must operate voltage climbs with temperature and is highest on a hot start, after the coil has been carrying current.

A single-side stable relay held on for long stretches without switching heats its own insulation, and a film can grow on the contacts until they become unreliable. For such duty use a latching (magnetic-holding) type; where a single-side stable type has to be used, the circuit should be fail-safe against contact failure or a burnt-out coil.
With a DC load, connect the common terminal, pin 7, to the positive side. The contact polarity sets how much material moves between the contacts and so how long they last.
Keep the coil polarity (+, −) as marked. When several relays sit close together on one board, the distance between terminals of neighbouring relays is at most two 2.54 mm pitches.

The relays are plastic sealed and can go through automatic soldering. Wash after soldering with water-based or alcohol-based solvent below 40°C, and do not drop a freshly soldered relay into a cold bath. Standard types must not be cleaned ultrasonically: resonance can burn out the coil or weld the contacts. The -U types are built for ultrasonic cleaning.

Signal switching in telecommunication equipment, office automation machines, industrial equipment and security equipment. The 1,500 V (10×160 μs) impulse rating across open contacts meets FCC part 68. Packed in sticks (tubes) for automatic insertion.
